SECTION: Chapter 3 | Article 10. Scholarships. Scholarship grants and all other forms of financial assistance shall be awarded in accordance with pertinent rules and regulations.
Article 10. Scholarships. Scholarship grants and all other forms of financial assistance shall be awarded in accordance with pertinent rules and regulations.

Sec. 1. Academic Scholars

1.1. Government and Private Company Scholarship. Scholarship and study grants by government and private companies or individuals are also available for needy and deserving students.

1.4. Only one (1) government/public office scholarship is allowed for every qualified scholar.

Sec. 2. Non-academic Scholars

2.1. Varsity Scholars. The university provides incentives to deserving and dedicated athletes. This scholarship is divided into:

2.1.1. Full Scholarship/Training Allowance: SCUAA medalists whether gold, silver or bronze; grade average of 2.0 for the semester immediately proceeding; and possess good moral character

2.1.2. Half Scholarship/Training Allowance: point contributors in SCUAA; SCUAA finalists; average grade of 2.5 and maximum grade of 2.0.

2.2. Advanced ROTC

2.3. Cultural and the Performing Arts

2.4. Band Member

2.5. Student Government (President)

2.6. Publication (Editor-in-Chief)

SECTION: Chapter 5 | Article 3. Institutional Student Programs and Services. These are programs and activities the University offers to facilitate the delivery of essential services to the students. It refers to the services and programs designed to proactively provide for the basic health, food, shelter, and safety concerns of students including students with special needs and disabilities.
Recommend alternatives/options, if necessary, for students who failed the admission requirements.

1.9. Administer psychological tests for students who have special cases.

Sec. 2. Scholarship and Financial Assistance Services

2.1. Disseminate information to students regarding the requirements for scholarship.

2.2. Monitor academic performance of all students scholars irrespective of the type of scholarship.

2.3. Facilitate processing of allowances and benefits of all scholars.

2.4. Conduct testing and interview among scholarship applicants.

2.5. Select student-scholars based on testing and interview.

Sec. 3. Food Services

3.1. Set criteria for safety and sanitary conditions of food outlets within the compound of the institution.

3.2. Coordinate with local government and health department for the maintenance of food services quality inside the university premises.

3.3. Periodically inspect food outlets for sanitation and hygiene.

3.4. Ensure that healthy meals are being served at the university canteen.

Sec. 4. Health Services

4.1. Inform medical/dental services to faculty and students.

4.2. Ensure that there are sufficient medicines and drugs in case of emergency.

B. ADMISSION REQUIREMENTS

The requirements listed below should be in PDF format for uploading in the LSPU Online Application System. The clear and readable documents to be uploaded will be verified and serve as the basis of qualifications.

NOTE: No original copies of documents will be asked during the admission process. Please keep them for the enrolment process.

1. College Qualification
   General Weighted Average (GWA)
   As stipulated in the LSPU Handbook 2021, the colleges may set their respective qualifications on the general weighted average (GWA) of students to be admitted to the program (board or non-board) in consideration of accommodation capacity and standards. For the list of programs and their respective GWA requirements, please see "Annex A" on page 4.

2. Documentary Requirements

   For First Year College (Freshmen) Applicants:
   a. Recent 2x2 ID Picture (white background)
   b. Birth Certificate (PSA/NSO)
   c. Certificate of Good Moral Character (with certification of current grade level and school year)
   d.

Participation Credits

1.3.1.2. Ranking and Percentage Ranking and Percentage Table (Level / Participation Level Points / Winning Level Additional Points [1st, 2nd, 3rd]):
International / 6 / 1.00, 0.50, 0.25
National / 5 / (none)
Regional / 4 / (none)
Provincial / 3 / (none)
Institutional / 2 / (none)
College/Department / 1 / (none)

1st place on points earned: 70% 2nd place on points earned: 60% 3rd place on points earned: 50%

1.3.2. Student-Achievement-Based Evaluation, thirty percent (30%). It refers to an athlete involved in increasing the importance of athletics in student’s welfare and development by means of role modeling and/or relative program that gives impact on student’s involvement.

Ranking and Percentage 1st place on student achievement: 30% 2nd place on student achievement: 20% 3rd place on student achievement: 10%

1.3.3. In case there shall be the same percentage earned for two (2) or three (3) nominees, then the Selection and Screening Committee shall reserve its rights to determine to whom the awards is to be given based on the objective of tis performance and conduct of panel interview.

1.4. Screening and Selection Process.
